title: Coherent composition of finite-coefficient pullback on strict systems
statement:
Let $A_1\leftarrow A_2\leftarrow\cdots$ be an inverse sequence of finite commutative rings and ring homomorphisms. Let $j:Y\to Z$, $h:Z\to W$ and $k:W\to V$ be arbitrary morphisms of schemes [def-pc-scheme]. Use fixed small representatives of their small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-size-convention]. Write $B_{T,n}=(A_n)_T$ for the constant ring sheaf and use its canonical inverse-image identifications, compatible with maps of coefficient rings [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf, prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-ring-map]. For each scheme $T$ let $\mathscr S_T$ be the abelian category of sequences of $B_{T,n}$-module sheaves $M_n$ with $B_{T,n+1}$-linear maps $M_{n+1}\to\operatorname{Res}_{B_{T,n+1}\to B_{T,n}}M_n$; morphisms commute with these maps and exactness is componentwise [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections]. Use the ordinary unbounded derived categories $D(\mathscr S_T)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. For each composite $f$ of the given scheme maps let $U_f:D(\mathscr S_{\mathrm{target}(f)})\to D(\mathscr S_{\mathrm{source}(f)})$ be the functor obtained by applying the exact finite-coefficient module inverse image levelwise and then termwise to complexes [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-exact, lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections].

The canonical module-pullback composition maps determine natural isomorphisms of derived-system functors
$$a_{h,k}:U_{k\circ h}\xrightarrow{\sim}U_hU_k.$$
For every complex of strict systems, this is represented by the termwise module comparison at every degree and coefficient level; these module comparisons commute with the semilinear transitions. Evaluation at level $n$ identifies $a_{h,k}$ with the canonical finite-coefficient derived comparison $c_{h,k}$ of [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-derived-pullback-composition]. For every $S\in D(\mathscr S_V)$,
$$U_j(a_{h,k}(S))\circ a_{j,k\circ h}(S)=a_{j,h}(U_kS)\circ a_{h\circ j,k}(S)$$
as morphisms in $D(\mathscr S_Y)$, under the canonical associator. This equality is induced by an equality of natural transformations on complexes of strict systems before localization. No normalization, boundedness, constructibility or flatness of $A_m\to A_n$ is assumed.
